# FINAL REPORT: Japanese and Korean Artists with Breakthrough Hits in July 2009-2012 ## Summary of Investigation Process I conducted searches for Japanese and Korean artists who had breakthrough hit singles released in July 2009, 2010, 2011, or 2012 after previous singles that underperformed. I performed multiple searches including: 1. General searches for breakthrough hits in July during these specific years 2. Searches for specific artists like Kyary Pamyu Pamyu and SISTAR 3. Searches for Korean artists with breakthrough patterns (EXID as a reference case) ## FINAL ANSWER ### Primary Finding: Kyary Pamyu Pamyu - July 2011 ✓ **Artist:** Kyary Pamyu Pamyu (きゃりーぱみゅぱみゅ) **Birth Date:** January 29, 1993 (born Kiriko Takemura) **Breakthrough Single:** "Pon Pon Pon" (ぽんぽんぽん) - **Release Date:** July 16, 2011 (music video), July 20, 2011 (iTunes digital release) **Background:** - Japanese fashion model, blogger, and singer - Career began in 2009 as a fashion blogger and model in Harajuku - Stage name combines "Kyari" (a nickname from school) with "Pamyu Pamyu" (chosen because it sounded cute) **Previous Underperforming Singles:** - Released two digital singles in 2010 as part of the Avex high school musician project - These early releases did not achieve commercial success or chart recognition **Breakthrough Success:** - "Pon Pon Pon" reached the top ten on Japan's Oricon music chart - The psychedelic music video went viral on YouTube, becoming an international phenomenon - As of 2012, the song sold over 1 million digital downloads - Set records for a Japanese song: reached #1 in Finland and #4 in Belgium - The viral success launched her career internationally **Musical Style:** - Electropop/J-pop - Written and produced by Yasutaka Nakata of Capsule - Incorporates kawaii and Decora culture aesthetics - The song was intentionally written to cheer people up after the March 11, 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami --- ### Secondary Finding: SISTAR - July 2011 ✓ **Artist:** SISTAR (씨스타) **Members:** Hyolyn, Bora, Soyou, and Dasom - Formed in 2010 by Starship Entertainment **Breakthrough Single:** "So Cool" (쏘쿨) - **Release Date:** July 21, 2011 **Background:** - Debuted on June 3, 2010 with "Push Push" **Previous Singles Performance:** - "Push Push" (June 2010) - peaked at #9 on Gaon Digital Chart (modest debut) - "Shady Girl" (August 2010) - performed better than debut but not a major hit - "How Dare You" (November 2010) - became their first number one single **Breakthrough Success:** - "So Cool" immediately topped Korean music charts upon release - Became the inaugural number one song on the Billboard Korea K-Pop Hot 100 chart after its launch on August 25, 2011 - Solidified their status as a top-tier girl group in Korea - Marked their transition from rising group to established act **Musical Style:** - K-pop, dance-pop - Known for summer-themed songs and powerful vocals **Note:** While SISTAR had achieved a #1 hit before "So Cool," this July 2011 release represented a significant elevation in their commercial success and industry standing. --- ### Additional Reference Case: EXID (Not July 2009-2012, but relevant pattern) **Artist:** EXID (이엑스아이디) **Debut:** February 2012 with "Whoz That Girl" - Peaked at #36 on Gaon Singles Chart **Subsequent Underperformance:** - "Every Night" (October 2012) - debuted at #43, sold 105,000 digital copies - Multiple singles in 2012-2013 failed to achieve significant success **Breakthrough:** "Up & Down" (August 2014, not July) - Originally failed to chart in top 100 - A fancam of member Hani went viral in October 2014 - Song eventually topped charts and won multiple music show awards **Relevance:** While not matching the July timeframe, EXID represents the clearest example of the "third single breakthrough after failures" pattern in K-pop during this era. --- ## Conclusion **Kyary Pamyu Pamyu's "Pon Pon Pon" (July 2011)** is the strongest and most definitive match for the search criteria: - Clear breakthrough hit released in July 2011 - Previous singles underperformed commercially - Represents a "third single" breakthrough pattern - Achieved both domestic (Oricon top 10) and international success - Viral phenomenon that launched her career **SISTAR's "So Cool" (July 2011)** is a secondary match that represents a significant career elevation in July 2011, though they had achieved prior chart success. No clear matches were found for July 2009, July 2010, or July 2012 that fit the specific pattern of breakthrough after multiple underperforming singles.
